pr_title: kvevent: refactor blocking buffer to use chunked linked list
pr_body:
This change updates `kvevent.blockingBuffer` to use a chunked linked list instead of a regular linked list. It also updates the benchmark we use to measure performance for this struct. Please see the commit messages for more info.

Results:
```
name          old time/op    new time/op    delta
MemBuffer-10     377ms ± 1%     511ms ± 0%  +35.54%  (p=0.000 n=8+9)

name          old alloc/op   new alloc/op   delta
MemBuffer-10    33.6MB ± 0%     0.4MB ± 3%  -98.93%  (p=0.000 n=9+10)

name          old allocs/op  new allocs/op  delta
MemBuffer-10       120 ±10%       111 ±11%   -6.86%  (p=0.030 n=10+10)

```

The chunked implementation writes exactly the same # of events as the old implementation, which is about ~1179330 events.

Fixes: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/84709
Fixes: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/84582
(for now...)

issue_context.title: changefeedccl: Reduce backfill impact on foreground latency
issue_context.body:
Investigation conducted by @nvanbenschoten shows significant impact on foreground SQL latency when executing backfills; [summary here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14eiwMtJd0Mk-voTjhJWj1YIBjPjsKjAAn-cizXTq45U/edit#heading=h.3ec2k2dcbmuq) (internal). The solution will be to reduce memory usage to reduce GC (assist) pressure.

- [x] Reduce default size of blocking buffer.  Suggested default of 1/8 of current default (125MB). 
  - https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/84686 
- [x] https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/86421
- [x] https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/87718 
- [x] https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/84709
- [x] https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/86469

Jira issue: CRDB-17745

Epic CRDB-24463
comments: I believe this issue is fixed now.

review_comments:
Turns out, this is entirely not needed; just implement Acquire (and ShouldWait) directly on Event;
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/86133/files#diff-917e22b7688547f6eaa760526364e4d208ed59ecc84876749dbb8176f234bff2L359

I just pushed https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/86133
I didn't think this benchmark was appropriate because it measures how fast it will take to fill up 64MB worth of blocking buffer; I'm not sure that's what we should be measuring.

The above branch executes the benchmark where many events are put into the buffer, and b.N events are consumed.
I was trying to simulate conditions described https://docs.google.com/document/d/14eiwMtJd0Mk-voTjhJWj1YIBjPjsKjAAn-cizXTq45U/edit# -- alas, not too successfully.  Still, running benchmark that puts in e.g. 40M events is more appropriate IMO.

The intention is that you run this benchmark with `-test.benchtime=45s` (or even 60s, also -show-logs is nice).
By specifying longer run time you test significant numbers of events being ingested in short time.  Also note, that there is a simulation of "sink flushing" -- i.e. allocations are released after 32MB of data has been accumulated (this is closer to what's described in the docs).

I think you should incorporate above benchmark version and rerun the benchmark against master and your updated version.  Please run at least for 45 seconds (or 1m); also, please run at least 10 times each iteration to produce final report.

Please note that I don't expect to see significant differences in either performance *OR* allocations.  The reason for this is that I don't that short benchmark durations give enough time for GC to really kick in...  You could try playing w/ longer durations; or perhaps higher producer concurrency and/or larger batches (64MB before releasing allocation ... or even higher).  You could also run w/ `GODEBUG=gctrace=1`  environment.

I still think this is a good change; In addition to this micro benchmark, we should also run the same test/setup as described in https://docs.google.com/document/d/14eiwMtJd0Mk-voTjhJWj1YIBjPjsKjAAn-cizXTq45U/edit#= to validate these changes.
